claims.statement: For an ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star with the contract polynomials and original tip multiplicities, at every actual eligible lower-half p (x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, 2p<=alpha), the guarded weighted-tip inequality W[p+1]C[p-1]<=W[p]C[p], W=sum_i r_i A_i, implies the actual strict selectors include a tip and imply selected MASS A=sum_i r_i e_i T_i[p-2]>=b delta D_j, with b=e0+sum_i r_i e_i, j=p-2, delta=q-j, D_j=Delta_j L^N. The implication uses the actual first strict parent descent, positive log-concave C=GQ, and the branchwise bound 2T_i[j]>=3delta D_j; it does not assume endpoint selection.
claims.scope: Conditional universal implication on the exact contract family and all actual eligible lower-half ranks, retaining integer zero extension, strict current-p selectors and original tag multiplicities. It proves no weighted-tip LR instance and has no arbitrary-tree extension.
claims.reason: The strict first descent makes C[p]/C[p-1]<1 by log-concavity after the rising binomial summand is removed. The assumed weighted comparison then forces Delta_p W<0 and at least one selected branch. Its multiplicity is at least 2; the accepted branchwise 3/2 payment pays b=B+e0 whether or not the endpoint selector is active. The proof and all guards are written in the report.

claims.statement: On the contract's actual eligible lower-half path-star rows, with t=C[j+1]/C[j] in (0,1), delta=q-j and kappa=1-t+t/delta, the accepted relative margin Delta_j T_i<=-kappa T_i[j] implies S=bD_j+sum_i r_i e_i Delta_j T_i<=bD_j-kappa A. Hence the exact-ratio payment kappa A>=bD_j implies S<=0, and the stronger selected MASS A>=b delta D_j implies that payment.
